new_candidates.body:
Observed on master at 0b3db8d7c5 (Linux, opt build). The output is identical
with #25125 applied.

**Repro** (two parses into one plant). This program compiles as is against
Drake.

```cpp
#include <exception>
#include <fstream>
#include <iostream>
#include <string>

#include <fmt/format.h>

#include "drake/common/temp_directory.h"
#include "drake/multibody/parsing/parser.h"
#include "drake/multibody/plant/multibody_plant.h"

using drake::multibody::MultibodyPlant;
using drake::multibody::Parser;

int main() {
  const std::string urdf = drake::temp_directory() + "/u.urdf";
  std::ofstream(urdf) << R"(<robot name='u'>
  <link name='R'/>
  <link name='B'/>
  <joint name='RB' type='fixed'><parent link='R'/><child link='B'/></joint>
</robot>)";
  MultibodyPlant<double> plant(0.0);
  Parser(&plant).AddModelsFromString(
      "<sdf version='1.12'><model name='m'><link name='X'/></model></sdf>",
      "sdf");
  std::cout << "First parse done." << std::endl;
  try {
    Parser(&plant, "pre")
        .AddModelsFromString(fmt::format(R"(<sdf version='1.12'>
  <model name='m'>
    <include merge='true'><uri>file://{}</uri><name>u</name></include>
    <link name='A'/>
  </model>
</sdf>)",
                                         urdf),
                             "sdf");
    std::cout << "Second parse done.\n";
  } catch (const std::exception& e) {
    std::cout << "Second parse threw: " << e.what() << "\n";
  }
  return 0;
}
```

**Output:**

```
First parse done.
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
  what():  std::bad_alloc
(core dumped)
```

- **Expected:** a model `pre::m` with links `A`, `R`, and `B`, or a
  diagnostic.
- **Actual:** the process terminates.

**Backtrace** (`gdb -batch -ex 'catch throw std::bad_alloc' -ex run -ex bt`,
opt build, so there are no line numbers):

```
#0  0x00007ffff6ebb35a in __cxa_throw () from /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libstdc++.so.6
#1  0x00007ffff6ea5ac8 in ?? () from /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libstdc++.so.6
#2  0x000055555602249b in drake_vendor::sdf::v0::Error::Implementation* drake_vendor::gz::utils::detail::DefaultCopyConstruct<drake_vendor::sdf::v0::Error::I...
#3  0x0000555555fa43fd in std::_Function_handler<void (drake_vendor::sdf::v0::InterfaceModelPoseGraph const&), drake::multibody::internal::(anonymous namespa...
#4  0x0000555556057efe in drake_vendor::sdf::v0::InterfaceModel::InvokeRepostureFunction(drake_vendor::sdf::v0::ScopedGraph<drake_vendor::sdf::v0::PoseRelati...
#5  0x0000555556081d2a in drake_vendor::sdf::v0::Model::SetPoseRelativeToGraph(drake_vendor::sdf::v0::ScopedGraph<drake_vendor::sdf::v0::PoseRelativeToGraph>...
#6  0x00005555560bbae3 in drake_vendor::sdf::v0::Root::Implementation::UpdateGraphs(drake_vendor::sdf::v0::Model&, std::vector<drake_vendor::sdf::v0::Error, ...
#7  0x00005555560be749 in drake_vendor::sdf::v0::Root::Load(std::shared_ptr<drake_vendor::sdf::v0::SDF>, drake_vendor::sdf::v0::ParserConfig const&) ()
#8  0x00005555560bf4bf in drake_vendor::sdf::v0::Root::LoadSdfString(std::__cxx11::basic_string<char, std::char_traits<char>, std::allocator<char> > const&, ...
#9  0x0000555555fb16cc in drake::multibody::internal::(anonymous namespace)::LoadSdf(drake::multibody::internal::SDFormatDiagnostic const&, drake_vendor::sdf...
#10 0x0000555555fc9074 in drake::multibody::internal::AddModelsFromSdf(drake::multibody::internal::DataSource const&, std::optional<std::__cxx11::basic_strin...
#11 0x0000555555fc9c9e in drake::multibody::internal::SdfParserWrapper::AddAllModels(drake::multibody::internal::DataSource const&, std::optional<std::__cxx1...
#12 0x0000555555df4b2c in drake::multibody::Parser::AddModelsFromString(std::__cxx11::basic_string<char, std::char_traits<char>, std::allocator<char> > const...
#13 0x0000555555df42f6 in main ()
```

**Root cause** (from code reading and the experiment below; not yet fixed).
Drake line numbers are for `multibody/parsing/detail_sdf_parser.cc` on master;
libsdformat line numbers are for the vendored `sdformat16_16.1.0`.
- Drake's custom model parser callback receives libsdformat's `sdf::Errors&`
  and passes its address on: `ParseNestedInterfaceModel(workspace, include,
  &errors, root_dir)` (:3039), which hands it to `ConvertToInterfaceModel()`
  (:2902).
- `ConvertToInterfaceModel()` builds the interface model's reposture function
  as a lambda that captures that `sdf::Errors*` by value (:2746-2757), and
  writes reposture errors through it with
  `PropagateErrors(std::move(inner_errors), errors)` (:2756).
- libsdformat calls the custom parser with a local `sdf::Errors errors;`
  scoped to one iteration of the loop over `CustomModelParsers()` in
  `loadIncludedInterfaceModels()` (`src/Utils.cc:288-289`), called from
  `Model::Load()` (`src/Model.cc:252`). That object is destroyed when the
  iteration ends.
- libsdformat invokes the reposture function later, while building the pose
  graphs in `Root::Load()`: `Root::Implementation::UpdateGraphs()`
  (`src/Root.cc:606`, `:617`) -> `Model::SetPoseRelativeToGraph()`
  (`src/Model.cc:944`, `:949`; also `src/World.cc:897`, and
  `Model::PrepareForMerge()` at `src/Model.cc:1296`) ->
  `InterfaceModel::InvokeRepostureFunction()` (`src/InterfaceModel.cc:161-170`).
  `RepostureFunction` is `std::function<void(const InterfaceModelPoseGraph&)>`
  (`include/sdf/InterfaceModel.hh:54-55`), so it has no error output of its
  own.
- So any reposture error is written through a dangling pointer. The observed
  `std::bad_alloc` while copying an `sdf::Error` is consistent with heap
  corruption; ASan should report a stack-use-after-scope.
- Even if the memory were valid, those errors would be lost: libsdformat
  copies the callback's errors into `allErrors` right after the callback
  returns (`src/Utils.cc:290-293`), so anything written later is never
  reported.
- The lambda repostures every body in `model_instance`
  (`plant->GetBodyIndices(model_instance)`, :2750), not only the bodies this
  interface model exported (`interface_model_helper.body_indices()`). In this
  repro that is the direct trigger: the merge include's instance is the
  earlier parse's `m`, so the lambda tries to resolve that parse's link `X`
  in the included model's pose graph and fails. It also calls
  `SetDefaultFloatingBaseBodyPose()` (:2757) on the earlier parse's bodies.

The merge include lands in the earlier, unprefixed instance `m` because of
the prefix problem in #25128. Any other reposture error would reach the same
dangling write.

**Experiment:** in the reposture lambda, I replaced
`PropagateErrors(std::move(inner_errors), errors);` with logging the errors.
The crash went away. The log showed the one reposture error, "Frame name [X]
not found in pose graph." for link `X`, and the second parse then threw an
ordinary diagnostic: "attached_to name[X] specified by frame with
name[_merged__u__model__] does not match a nested model, link, joint, or
frame name in model with name[m]."

**Suggested fix:**
- Don't let the reposture function hold the custom parser callback's
  `sdf::Errors`. Report reposture errors through something that outlives
  `Root::Load()`, such as a pointer to `workspace.diagnostic`, which
  `AddModelsFromSdf()` holds across `LoadSdf()`. Not the callback's `errors`,
  and not `ParseNestedInterfaceModel()`'s local `subdiagnostic` (:2822), which
  captures the same `errors` (:2826).
- Repose only the bodies the interface model exported: copy
  `interface_model_helper.body_indices()` into the lambda.
- Optionally, ask upstream libsdformat for a `RepostureFunction` overload that
  takes an `sdf::Errors&`.
- Separately, merge includes shouldn't go into a model instance from an
  earlier parse (#25128).
